questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to win at Monopoly
The history and religious meaning of the seven deadly sins
The psychology of greed and how wealth can change people
Why expensive gifts make people happy
questions.why: They discuss greed, a psychology experiment with Monopoly, and how wealth affects empathy.

questions.q: Do Neil and Beth agree about greed at the start?
options: Yes, they both think greed is bad
No – Neil says greed is good, but Beth isn't so sure
Yes, they both think greed is natural and good
No – Beth says greed is good, but Neil strongly disagrees
questions.why: Neil says “Greed is good!” and Beth replies, “I'm not so sure” and mentions the deadly sins.

questions.q: According to Neil, how does greed work in the brain?
options: It's in the reward centre, mostly unconscious
It is controlled by careful, logical thinking
It only happens when we are tired
It happens in the part of the brain that controls memory
questions.why: He says greed is controlled by the reward centre, at the unconscious, emotional level.

questions.q: How was Professor Paul Piff's Monopoly game made unfair?
options: The poor player was not allowed to buy houses
The rich player was allowed to look at the other player's cards
The game was played without any money
The rich player rolled two dice and got double money at Go
questions.why: The rich player rolled two dice and collected twice as much when passing Go.

questions.q: How did the “rich” players explain why they won?
options: They said the game was unfair
They said their own decisions had led to their success
They said they were just lucky
They thanked the poor player and said the game was close
questions.why: Piff says they took credit, talking about how their decisions led to victory.

questions.q: Why does Professor Piff mention “that flip of a coin”?
options: To explain how the game started each time
To show that the poor players had been cheating during the game
To stress that the players' advantage came from pure chance
To suggest a new rule for Monopoly
questions.why: He contrasts their claims with the random coin flip that gave them privilege.

questions.q: What does Piff admit about real life?
options: Everyone who is rich was simply lucky
The experiment shows perfectly how wealth works in real life
Poor people never work hard
Some people really do succeed through their own hard work
questions.why: He says some people have worked themselves up and get what they have because they worked hard.

questions.q: According to Piff, why might wealthy people have less empathy?
options: They depend less on other people
They work too many hours
They spend too much time playing games
They are always worried about money
questions.why: He says well-off people don't need others as much, so their empathy might suffer.
